trigger: Board srcWithMext shows SEG high digits 0x374 instead of 0x378 while Verilator passes, indicating four M-extension subtests fail only on FPGA.

files_modified.notes: Changed DIV_0 result unpacking to match Vivado 2023.2 div_gen remainder-mode output: quotient is m_axis_dout_tdata[63:32], remainder is [31:0].
Changed the Verilator behavior model to emit m_axis_dout_tdata as {quotient, remainder}, matching generated Vivado DIV_0 demo testbench behavior.
Documented the DIV_0 output packing contract, the Vivado demo testbench evidence, and the board symptom where srcWithMext reaches 0x374xxxxx instead of 0x378xxxxx.
Recorded the DIV_0 packing alignment fix and verification evidence.

verification: Generated a temporary Vivado 2023.2 DIV_0 div_gen IP with the current Tcl parameters. Its demo_tb/tb_DIV_0.vhd assigns remainder <= m_axis_dout_tdata(31 downto 0) and quotient <= m_axis_dout_tdata(63 downto 32).
make sim-rv32 SUITE=rv32um BUILD_JOBS=4 OBJCACHE= passed all 8 rv32um tests: div, divu, mul, mulh, mulhsu, mulhu, rem, remu.

make sim-src TEST=srcWithMext MAX_CYCLES=500000000 BUILD_JOBS=4 OBJCACHE= reached SEG last_nonzero_raw=0x37800000 with mext_count_from_seg=8; it timed out before the final pass marker because the 500M-cycle cap was below this build's full runtime.
notes: Root cause: the previous RTL and Verilator DIV_0 model were self-consistently wrong, both treating [31:0] as quotient and [63:32] as remainder. Verilator therefore passed, while FPGA used the real Vivado div_gen packing and caused DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU subtests to fail. Rebuild the Vivado project or regenerate DIV_0 before producing a new bitstream.

trigger: srcSmoke failed with SEG=0 after branch recovery; VCD showed x8 was renamed to p0 after a JAL redirect although the frame-pointer addi had committed.

files_modified.notes: Only retirement entries that allocated a destination physical register now drive commit_arch_o/commit_prd_o to RenameUnit. Non-writing uops keep commit_valid_o for retire/perf/store-buffer purposes but no longer update aRAT with pseudo rd bits.
Recorded the aRAT commit-map corruption fix and the intended verification cascade.

verification: CCACHE_DISABLE=1 make verilator-build BUILD_JOBS=2 completed successfully after the CommitUnit aRAT fix.

python3 scripts/run_verilator.py src --test srcSmoke --no-build --max-cycles 200000 --trace reached rv32i_pass_counter_last=37, rv32i_fail_counter_last=0, seg.last_nonzero_raw=0x37000000, then timed out due to the short cycle cap.

python3 scripts/run_verilator.py src --test srcWithMext --no-build --max-cycles 2000000000 failed at 681736299 cycles with final fail lamp marker. Result archived at docs/archive/2026-07-10/052_srcWithMext_full_result.md. Key fields: SEG=0x37613634, expected high=0x37800000, rv32i_pass_counter=37, rv32i_fail_counter=0, mext_count_from_seg=6/8.
notes: Root cause: store and branch instructions still carry instruction bits in the decoded rd field. CommitUnit previously forwarded that field to RenameUnit whenever commit_valid_o was high, so a store such as fe042423 could update aRAT[x8] to p0. A later branch/JAL recovery restored sRAT from the corrupted aRAT, causing loads using x8 as a base to address 0xffffffdc instead of the stack frame.

trigger: Vivado/Tcl IP integration review found IROM_0 Dual_Port_ROM B-port clock mismatch and stale DIV_0 packing documentation.

files_modified.notes: Set IROM_0 CONFIG.Assume_Synchronous_Clk to true for the same-clock dual-port ROM contract.
Connected IROM_0.clkb to w_cpu_clk so the top-level instance matches Vivado blk_mem_gen Dual_Port_ROM wrapper ports.
Added clkb to the Verilator dual-port ROM model and clocked B-port address capture from clkb.
Documented IROM A/B clocking and corrected DIV_0 quotient/remainder packing.
Updated IROM timing contract to include clka/clkb and same-clock top-level wiring.
Recorded the Vivado IP integration fix.

verification: python3 -m json.tool docs/rtl_changes.json passed after converting the manifest to a JSON array.
git diff --check passed for the current IROM/Vivado documentation changes.

Static reference scan found no stale single-port IROM signal names in docs/fpga/ip_timing_alignment.md, docs/fpga/vivado_project.md, rtl/soc/student_top.sv, rtl/ip/IROM_0.sv, or fpga/create_vivado_project.tcl.

python3 scripts/run_verilator.py src --test srcSmoke --build --max-cycles 200000 rebuilt the src/student_top Verilator target after the IROM clkb change, then timed out as expected at the short cap with rv32i_pass_counter=37, rv32i_fail_counter=0, and SEG=0x37000000.
notes: Vivado 2023.2 blk_mem_gen_v8_4 component metadata enables clkb for non-single-port native memories including Dual_Port_ROM. Its changelog states common_clock internally connects clkb to clka but preserves the interface, so both clocks must be wired to the same source.
